title: Chairo paceño (Bolivian beef, chuño and vegetable soup)

ingredients.name: chuño (freeze-dried potato) soaked overnight, or 2 small potatoes as substitute
white corn kernels or cooked hominy
chopped parsley and mint, with a pinch of oregano

steps: Soak the wheat berries or barley for 2 hours. Brown the beef lightly in the oil with the onion and garlic.
Add the water and soaked grain, bring to a boil and simmer for 45 minutes until the beef begins to soften.
Add the chuño or substitute potato, corn and carrot and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes, peas and fava beans and cook another 15 minutes until everything is tender.
Season with salt and pepper, and sprinkle with parsley and mint before serving.

title: Fricasé paceño (La Paz-style pork and hominy soup)

ingredients.name: pork ribs or pork shoulder, in pieces
small potatoes, or 4 chuño soaked overnight

steps: Season the pork with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the pork lightly.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until soft, then stir in the ají paste, cumin and oregano.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil and simmer, covered, for 45 to 60 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the crumbled bread to thicken the broth and stir. Add the hominy and potatoes and cook for 20 more minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve in deep bowls sprinkled with parsley, with bread on the side.

title: Llajua (Bolivian fresh hot tomato and locoto sauce)

ingredients.name: fresh hot red peppers (locotos), or 2 jalapeños or small red chillies

steps: Place the tomatoes and chillies in a small pan with a splash of water and cook gently for 5 minutes until just soft; this step is optional, as traditional llajua is often raw.
Remove the seeds from the chillies for a milder sauce, then crush them together with the tomatoes using a mortar and pestle or a short blitz in a blender.
Add the coriander, garlic if using, salt and water, and mix to a coarse, juicy purée.
Taste and add more salt or chilli. Serve at once with grilled meat, salteñas, potatoes or empanadas.

title: Mocochinchi (Bolivian dried peach and cinnamon drink)

ingredients.name: dried peaches (mocochinchi), or dried apricots as substitute

steps: Rinse the dried peaches and soak them in the water overnight until plump.
Pour the fruit and its water into a pot, add the cinnamon, cloves and orange peel and bring to a boil.
Add the sugar and simmer for 30 minutes until the liquid is amber and the fruit is soft.
Cool and chill thoroughly. Serve cold in glasses with a peach in each glass.

title: Pique macho (Bolivian beef, sausage and fries party platter)

ingredients.name: hot yellow chillies (locotos or ají amarillo), sliced
mustard, mayonnaise and ketchup to serve

steps: Season the beef with cumin, salt and pepper. Fry the chips in hot oil until golden and crisp and keep them warm in the oven.
Sear the beef strips in a hot pan with oil for 4 to 5 minutes until browned, then remove.
In the same pan, fry the sausage slices until browned.
Add the onion, tomato, pepper and chillies and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes, still keeping some bite.
Pile the chips on a large platter and top with the beef, sausage and vegetables. Add the halved eggs and drizzle over the mustard, mayonnaise and ketchup.
Serve with plenty of napkins, to share with beer or cold drinks.

title: Salteñas (Bolivian juicy baked beef and potato pasties)

ingredients.name: ají amarillo paste, or 2 tsp mild chilli paste
powdered gelatine, dissolved in 4 tbsp hot water

steps: Make the filling one day ahead: cook the onion in a little oil with the ají paste, cumin, oregano and salt until soft.
Add the stock and simmer for 5 minutes, then stir in the dissolved gelatine and fold in the beef, potatoes and peas. Chill overnight so the filling sets into a firm jelly.
Mix the flour, sugar, salt, melted butter, egg yolks and warm water into a smooth, firm dough; rest it for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thin and cut 12 cm circles. Place a heaped spoonful of cold filling in each, fold over into a half-moon and seal the edge by pinching and folding a decorative rope.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 220 C for 15 to 18 minutes until golden. Rest 5 minutes and eat carefully, as the juice inside is hot.

title: Sándwich de chola (La Paz pulled roast pork sandwich)
steps: Rub the pork with garlic, cumin, oil and salt and leave it for 2 hours or overnight.
Roast at 160 C in a covered pan with the beer for about 3 hours until the meat is tender, then uncover and brown for 20 minutes. Rest and slice or shred.
Mix the carrot, onion, vinegar, hot pepper and a pinch of salt and leave for 15 minutes to quick-pickle.
Split the rolls and fill them generously with warm pork and its juices.
Top with the pickled vegetables and serve with llajua.

title: Silpancho (Cochabamba-style breaded beef over rice and potatoes with fried egg)

ingredients.name: thin beef steaks (about 100 g each), pounded very thin

steps: Season the pounded beef with salt, pepper and garlic powder. Dip each steak in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs.
Fry the steaks in hot oil for about 2 minutes per side until crisp and cooked through. Drain.
Make the salad by mixing tomato, onion, beetroot, parsley, vinegar and a pinch of salt.
On each plate, spread a layer of rice, then a layer of sliced potatoes, then lay a steak on top.
Fry the 4 eggs and place one on each steak, then spoon the salad over the top. Serve with llajua if you like.

title: Trancapecho (Cochabamba rice, breaded beef and egg in a bread roll)

ingredients.name: bread rolls or flat bread tortillas
llajua and oil for frying, salt and pepper

steps: Season the steaks, dip in beaten egg, coat in breadcrumbs and shallow-fry for about 2 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Mix the tomato and onion with vinegar and a pinch of salt for a quick salad.
Split the rolls or warm the flat breads and layer in rice, fried potato slices, a breaded steak, a fried egg and salad.
Close the sandwiches and serve immediately with llajua on the side.
